title: Locality-aware fail-fast gate and sticky fallback reconciler
author: Priya Khatri
description:
Motivation: Regional tail latency spikes (mostly in noisy EU/Beta zones) cause downstream SLO violations and frequent fallback oscillation. Current failover logic is purely reactive and global, which leads to cross-region thrash and unnecessary cold-starts. This PR introduces a locality-aware fail-fast gate combined with a sticky fallback reconciler to reduce oscillation and improve SLO stability without increasing overall error budgets.

Summary of changes: 1) locality fail-fast gate: a lightweight per-locality admission gate that evaluates short-window tail latency (p95/p99) and error rates, and triggers a fast-fail decision for requests that are likely to miss the SLO. The gate uses an exponential moving average with configurable hysteresis to avoid flip-flops. 2) sticky fallback reconciler: when a locality decides to fallback to a pre-warmed compatible model variant or remote region, the reconciler records a short sticky decision per-tenant (default 30s) and coordinates backfills of KV/cache where applicable. Sticky decisions are opportunistically refreshed or allowed to expire based on health probes. 3) speculative regional fallback: for requests routed from latency-sensitive tenants, we introduce speculative fallback attempts to warm remote replicas asynchronously while continuing local servicing; this reduces cold-start impact on the first fallback. 4) Observability: new telemetry (locality_failfast_decisions, sticky_fallback_events, speculative_warmup_success) and annotated traces for decision paths. 5) Feature flag + knob surface: runtime flags and per-tenant override (console + API) to tune thresholds, sticky TTL, and speculative concurrency.

Why this is different: instead of global thresholds we track locality characteristics and apply hysteresis with sticky decisioning so the system degrades gracefully and remains predictable. The reconciler coordinates KV preservation during short fallbacks so client-level caches see fewer regressions.

Testing & results: Unit tests added for gate logic, hysteresis transitions, reconciler state machine. Integration tests exercise cross-region fallback and speculative warm path. Canary in us-west with synthetic tail spike showed 38% reduction in fallback flip rate and 22% fewer cold-start latencies on first fallback attempt. p99 latency for affected tenants improved by ~120ms during injected noisy-driver tests.

Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged rollout to 10% of requests (per-tenant sampling) for two days; 2) progressive increase to 50% with close telemetry monitoring; 3) enable per-tenant sticky TTL tuning for enterprise tenants only during phase 2. Rollback path: disable feature flag or reduce sampled tenants to 0; reconciler state timeouts ensure no long-lived inconsistent state.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for gate and reconciler - [x] Integration test for speculative warm path - [x] Added metrics and dashboard proposals - [x] Feature flag gating + console controls - [x] Run canary with synthetic spike harness - [x] Security review (auth boundary unchanged)

Related: Linear ENG-1345 (regional tail stabilization), ENG-2109 (sticky fallback design). Support ticket SUP-4421 was the immediate trigger for the investigation.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps decision logic deterministic and small—no ML-based heuristics—to reduce risk during rollout. Future work: cost-aware fallback ranking and automated TTL tuning based on tenant historical stability.

review_comments: Ethan: Can you clarify how the hysteresis window reacts to sustained but slowly improving latency? Suggest adding an exponential fallback to decay the threshold.
Author (Priya): Hysteresis uses an EMA with configurable alpha; added comments and test cases covering slow decay. We decided against exponential fallback for now to keep behavior predictable.
Marta: Sticky TTL defaults to 30s — is that empirically derived? Could be short for some enterprise flows.
Author: Default 30s chosen from canary tuning; made TTL configurable per-tenant and added console knob. Documented recommended values in ops guide.
Noah: One unit test flaky on CI (TestReconcilerBackoff) — looks timing sensitive.
Author: Increased test tolerance and replaced real time.Sleep with a controllable clock in the reconciler tests. Re-ran CI.
Ethan: Approved pending CI green and a short ops runbook addition.

release_notes: Introduce locality-aware fail-fast gate and sticky fallback reconciler. Improves regional SLO stability by reducing fallback oscillation and cold-starts. Feature-flagged and disabled by default. See docs/ops/locality-failfast-guide.md for configuration and rollout steps.
